newsitem.title: UK: IGC conference warned of food security concerns.
newsitem.headline: IGC conference warned of food security concerns.

text.p: Increasing trade liberalisation that shifts food production to the more efficient suppliers carries risks for food security, according to a former Japanese vice-minister of agriculture, Hirofumi Ueno.

"I acknowledge the argument, made by many exporting countries, that food security is achieved by pursuing trade liberalisation and shifting production to the countries with comparative advantages in agriculture," Ueno told the International Grains Council's conference in London.

"However, I cannot completely agree with this argument because the concentration of food production in the region with a comparative advantage would accelerate the dependence on a small number of exporting countries and increase the risk of a food shortage caused by severe weather and accident in food shipment," Ueno said.
The rules for international food trade should allow individual governments to ensure stable food supplies, he said.
He pointed out that exporting countries' reluctance to accept discipline on export restrictions indicate their difficulty in following free trade principles in relation to basic foodstuffs.
